STRUCTURE OF TASK-VECTOR INTERFERENCE IN
MERGED LANGUAGE MODELS
Chencheng Zhu
UNSW Sydney
chencheng.zhu@student.unsw.edu.au
ABSTRACT
Model merging by task arithmetic works until it doesn’t, and the field diagnoses why with magnitudes: layerwise
representation bias, deviations from cross-task linearity, parameter overlap. Tracking the exact layerwise cross-term of
merged LLMs through a factorial ledger and intervening on it directly, we find that magnitude is insufficient—and
inconsistent across model families—as a diagnostic axis. An exact decomposition of the layerwise flux shows it is
dominated by amplifying transport of the existing cross-term (∼65–70% in both model families, gain >1 per lat
block), and erasing the term is undone by propagation—rebuilt to 99% of its norm at cosine 0.99—unless applied near
the output; a basin test (six starting displacements, including 2× overshoot and four structured wrong directions, all
reconverging at cosine 0.83–0.99) establishes the carried direction as an attractor of the forward pass. That direction
is causally load-bearing: erasure along it removes expressed interference dose-dependently and saturates at exact
erasure, norm-matched wrong-direction controls fail or backfire, and instruction wrappers gate the effect—the same
erasure finds 13× less relative interference to remove under a wrapper that internally amplifies the cross-term (the
wrapper drowns the interaction in a template-pinned main effect rather than shrinking it). Magnitude, by contrast,
is at best a coarse correlate: float32 local generation tracks pair ordering only loosely, every magnitude metric we
measure (local, cumulative, parameter-space, representation bias) points the wrong way across formats, and the
striking ±15% “universality” of naive bf16 generation turns out to be quantization roughness—a cautionary result
we document. Notably, task pairs whose local cross-term generation differs by at most 1.9× differ by 14×–337×
in causally removable interference. All 46 predictions were preregistered and frozen before their data; falsifications,
including of our own headline expectations, are reported as such. Reduced replications at a second family and a larger
scale reproduce the causal structure at all three model points. Format-wrapped evaluations, we conclude, read the
gate—not the interference.
